User 1: I just went on facebook for a little bit and saw your comment on my post. Since you said you want to talk privately, I am sending you this message. This is all I’m going to say on the matter and I urge you to really think about it. Like I said, I have some nonnegotiable values and everything I am about to say, i believe in so strongly based on my self reflection, my values and what I know to be true that I can not waste my energy debating them anymore. I can’t argue with you about whether civilians deserve to be shot in the street because to me, it’s SO clearly wrong. We could get into the weeds about why ICE was acting unlawfully to begin with or the evidence that I’ve SEEN (not propaganda) that proves Sarah Jenkins was not trying to harm him but honestly none of that matters— this administration wants us to keep arguing over the facts and what we see with our own eyes to distract from the real issue— that this administration and its followers have lost their humanity in pursuit of power or “righteousness”. 

I will say this: when it’s someone killed by the cops, they pull out their criminal record, as if that gives the state a right to kill someone in the street. when it’s a US citizen killed by ICE, it’s “she should have just complied”. when it’s children being killed at school, it’s “a price to pay for our second amendment rights”. For a “pro-life” party to consistently jump at the chance to justify senseless violence, is so hypocritical.

Undocumented immigrants pay taxes. Undocumented immigrants statistically commit crimes at a lower rate than US citizens. DHS is spending BILLIONS of dollars on ICE operations. So it’s not about crime, it’s not about the economy, it’s about dehumanizing a group of people and creating a common enemy to use to their advantage. I care about people and the decisions this administration is making does not align with what is best for any person in this country except themselves, in any way you cut it. I really hoped that you would see that and it honestly breaks my heart that you don’t but like I said, I won’t argue with anyone anymore about whether our government should be held accountable for its actions. No formal investigation was conducted. The state was blocked from investigating. The president and vice president put out a statement before any due diligence was done. If they truly thought the ICE agent was in the right, what would be the harm in investigating fully? Isn’t that the point of checks and balances? To make sure that each branch is acting ethically within their jurisdiction? 

Lastly, my friend, a US citizen was just stopped by ICE the other day because she is hispanic. They raided the building she was working in and only stopped people of color, as if white people can’t be immigrants. She said it was terrifying. They kept asking her where she was born, even though that doesn’t determine your citizenship. They’re looking for any reason to say they had cause to detain you. She said she was lucky she always travels with her passport. At the end of the day, you can’t say what you would do if 5 masked armed men ran up on your vehicle shouting profanities at you, especially as a woman. And ultimately, I just believe we should hold the government agents that our tax dollars are paying for to a higher standard than random civilians.

You said it saddens you that your grandchildren will grow up in this world being taught it’s ok to be violent towards law enforcement. It saddens me to have to teach Leo to fear law enforcement, the people who are supposed to help us. To tell him that he needs to comply with every order, even if it’s unlawful, so he doesn’t get hurt. To explain to him that black or brown friends that he has will be targeted by law enforcement more than him and if that ever happens, it might be his responsibility to protect them. That I will have to explain to Leo, a little boy so full of joy and love, that there is so much hatred in this world towards people who look, love, or worship differently than him. Especially since those “different” people are his friends at daycare, his aunts and uncles, people he cares about. I can only hope that we can instill love, acceptance and empathy in him enough that he will help better our society as he grows up.  I hope the world he lives in doesn’t require people to stand up to law enforcement because our government is acting unethically. 

User 2: We can agree that innocent people should not be "shot in the street".  Also, innocent kids should not be shot in school.  Teach Leo to respect, not fear law enforcment.  Your friend is smart to keep ID with her.

I mean, we agree but we disagree on how we see things. I always bring up what you call what about isms because there's contradiction and hypocrisy in how the left wants to apply rights.  For instance, the left is okay with protesters just being completely idiotic, blowing their whistles, harassing ice agents, threatening ice agents etc etc and they think that they can do this without consequences. Meanwhile, if someone wants to protest let's say some things that are being taught in schools and they go to a school board meeting to speak their mind, they are silenced and sometimes arrested. People should be able to peacefully protest of course. But I think these ice protesters are getting beyond peaceful.  Can we agree that people should not be following ice agents around, breaking into their vehicles and provoking them by making threatening statements to them?  To be honest, they are trying to impede them and that's not right.

User 1: I think it’s important to stand up against what is right.  Following ICE, blowing whistles, being “idiotic” is not a crime. I think it’s a crime that my friend, a law abiding American citizen, should even have to worry about traveling domestically with her federal ID because she knows she will be racially profiled by a government agency. She’s not “smart”, she’s scared. 

 I think our government should be held to a higher standard than random civilians. This administration is using unchecked power to carry out its agenda and frankly, it’s unconstitutional, morally corrupt and unethical. So, right now, I think there is no “right” way to react to an unjust government. If the power is in the people, like it should be, and the government has taken away the people’s voice, what else are they supposed to do? Unfortunately, this administration has created their own problems with the way they have behaved against the people’s best interests and clearly, following the law and the “right way” to do things hasn’t worked. So still, I blame the government for blocking any sort of accountability or checks and balances for its own or its agents actions. 

User 1: I know you said you don’t want to argue on facebook but it’s really hard for me to watch you post divisive and misleading information online and not respond. I love you dad but my heart is literally breaking for this country and i can’t be quiet about it. I hope you understand the need to stand up for what I think is right.

he said the state can’t prosecute federal against “who have absolute immunity”. he didn’t say that states can’t prosecute federal agents because that’s the job of the federal government. Because the Trump Administration uses words like “criminal illegal aliens” “Left wing radical lunatics” to make anyone who doesn’t fit their idea of the perfect law abiding citizen “less than”. And this is why i can’t have this conversation because once you decide these people are deserving of inhumane treatment, it doesn’t matter the context or circumstances

I think what's confusing for people of my generation is that your generation is just making up language and rules and laws that you think are immoral and trying to force feed us into going along with it and otherwise calling us names, calling us crazy etc.  In a way, you're dehumanizing us. User 1: If there really is a grand conspiracy, and Trump is currently in charge with all the resources at his disposal, why haven’t they been able to find a shred of evidence? 




 my first thought watching this was the language they chose to use. The reporter used very charged language the entire way through. Labeling every person they talked to as “agitators” even if the video footage did not reflect that. Again, i understand that most media or news is going to be biased, they obviously came here with a mission but the bias is so obvious that it makes me immediately question the reliability of the narrator. 

second, their comments about the car they’re driving and how protestors think they’re ICE also interested me because it represents a larger issue that they fail to touch on AT ALL. does it not bother you that armed federal agents can drive around in unmarked vehicles? when we talk about protestors “complying” and “respecting law enforcement” but law enforcement isn’t even clearly distinguished, to me that is a public safety risk? Not only for random civilians/protestors but obviously for this reporter as well.

Other than that, I don’t see what’s wrong with non profit organizations organizing protests and advocating for the issues they care about. That is a huge part of the activism space, on both sides of the political spectrum. That is usually even apart of the mission statement of non profit groups. The report threw some numbers on the screen about government grant funding but failed to make clear how that correlated to unethical or disingenuous behavior on the behalf of these non profits. We also don’t know if the people representing the non profits are being paid to be at the protest, or if they are just representing that organization as a volunteer. It seemed the reporter hoped that you would see the money and fill in the blanks that he was unable to provide with your own biases. He even makes it the title which I found very misleading. 

I think what you think I would be appalled at is the behavior of some of the protestors. Do I think they were being unnecessarily aggressive at times? Yes. Do I think death threats and following the camera crew is warranted? No. Is that the way I would conduct myself? Again no. But do I think this proves any grand conspiracy or undermines the legitimacy of the issues people are protesting. No. Much like the Black Panther’s activity didn’t undermine the legitimacy of the civil rights movement or warrant violence towards Martin Luther King. 

Do I support the protestors throwing things at the camera crew. Again no. But the reporter makes a HUGE leap to say “anyone who is not on their side will be destroyed or killed.” Up until the anonymous text, NONE of the evidence pointed to that. And even the anonymous text, do I think that was 100% wrong? Yes. Does one single text suddenly represent sentiments and demeanors of thousands of protestors. No. At best, their evidence for the very extreme statement of “anyone who is not on their side will be destroyed or killed” is flimsy, at worst, its intentional fear-mongering. In 3 days of undercover reporting they can’t even identify who “they” are outside of, in their own words “a few non profit organizations loosely tied together by ideology”. 

They also conveniently glossed over being hit with rubber bullets and tear gas with absolutely no explanation. From the footage right before, it didn’t seem like anyone was being particularly violent when the ICE agents decided to use riot control tactics against civilians. I would’ve loved for them to use their undercover cameras to expose what was happening there but perhaps there was no reason or it didn’t fit their narrative. 

In terms of the altercations with the protestors and the camera crew, the protestors kept repeating “don’t let them take your picture” and warning others that they are not genuine protestors. It’s telling to me that that is the warning. No calls to violence or even threats of bodily injury. People are afraid of being doxxed, losing their jobs or arrested for being apart of a protest against the government. Which i always thought was a little silly but this report actually showed me that fear is kind of valid since they recognized Linda Chen at the beginning and literally put all of her business into the report and then said she was at risk of losing her job because of her activism. and they also said the camera crew went through the hidden footage to identify people they talked to to sent to law enforcement. At the end, the reporter says “the first amendment is dead” because of the protestors pushing them to leave.

The first amendment: “Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.”

The first amendment protects our right to free speech against government prosecution, not against social consequences that may come with it from other civilians not liking what you have to say. Again, I would argue by him purposefully trying to record people’s faces to send to law enforcement is more of an attempt to violate free speech than anything he experienced. And the fact is, people already feel their first and second amendment rights are being violated because of what has happened in Minneapolis and the government’s reactions and statements to it. Is that not infringement of first amendment rights? Fear of arrest or persecution by the government for simply being at a protest, even if you don’t participate in any illegal activity that may or may not be happening? 

Then the part that really lost all credibility for me: when the protestors were trying to figure out their press association, one girl said she looks up a news organization that she thought was them and said “you’re not political at all”.  Then the narration says “What dawned on me in that moment is that it wasn’t a good thing that we weren’t political, it was actually a liability. if you’re not a member of their team, if you don’t believe exactly what they believe, you are their enemy. even if you are neutral you must be destroyed or killed”  

LITERALLY WHERE DID THEY SAY THAT!?!? Political does not mean specifically left or right. The definition of political is as followed: 

-relating to the government or the public affairs of a country.

-relating to the ideas or strategies of a particular party or group in politics.

-interested in or active in politics.

-motivated or caused by a person's beliefs or actions concerning politics.
I can understand how it would feel strange for a non political (as in a press organization that does not report on politics) to be boots on the ground in a hostile situation like this. This was the biggest reach ever to support his narrative that was NOT supported by the footage he put out and he just hoped people would fill in the blanks with their own biases and take the leap with them. Extremely irresponsible. 

The altercations at the end also just felt especially ironic to me. As they are being harassed by protestors, the camera crews say things like: 

“i’m showing my face, im not ICE” (Crazy that our tax payers are allowing masked gun men to roam the streets and that someone’s defense against being ICE would be the fact that they are showing their face)

“we’re american citizens” (Again, this is something that doesn’t stop being from being detained by ICE but yet they feel like it should provide them with some sort of protection. If you don’t believe ICE is detaining US citizens, look into Judge Kavanaugh’s rulings about whether ICE is allowed to detain people based on racial profiling). 

“it was impossible to convince them you are not ICE” (Again, it is the government’s responsibility to identify federal agents, especially those who are armed with lethal weapons but instead they are sewing seeds of chaos and fear of anyone who looks like they could be ICE. Why are people so afraid of ICE? Could it be that 2 Americans citizens died this month at the hands of ICE?)

Then the guy boils this all down to greed and money and power? Again, I don’t know where any of that is coming from because in this entire report, he has not proven that any of those are a motivator for any of the protestors. Many people just said “thanks for showing up for your community”. 

Is America headed for a civil war? perhaps. I hope not but that’s why i feel so anxious. If our country is irreconcilably divided, it’s due to biased disingenuous propaganda like this report and the government’s inability to protect the people they are supposed to service. If tensions are high, the government should be finding ways to diffuse things. If people are scared, the government should be a voice of reason and assurance instead of stoking the flames. Whether it is pure incompetency or intentional division, the Trump Administration is failing its people and the citizens are exercising their first amendment right to show up to protests and express that.  

People love to point to the numbers of people deported under Obama and Biden. So if the federal government IS capable of deporting dangerous criminals, faster, more efficiently, for less money AND without scaring people, what is the real reason for what the Trump administration is doing right now? Why is it costing SO much money and now, human life? 

His monologue about “power disparity” and lack of accountability is true. But again, I am failing to see where and when the power is lying with the “agitators”. The protests are happening to ask for accountability for the federal agents who have killed civilians. Yet, Trump and his administration put out statements like they were fact before either investigation has concluded. How is that accountability? Where is the true power and money right now? It’s certainly not random non profit organizations with left leaning ideologies or the American civilians who are taking to the streets hoping to be heard by their government.



Task:


Can you summarize both user's general argument throughout the text thread?

This text thread features a heated debate between two users, User 1 and User 2, who appear to be in a familial relationship (User 1 refers to User 2 as "dad").
